reason: Owns alias resolution and reports available names on a miss, but resolve_command still re-derives argv by split_whitespace on the configured command, so quoting is lost (crates/effigy-exec/src/alias.rs:100).

host_to_container canonicalises and refuses an outside path; container_to_host now maps an empty remainder to the host repo root, but still joins the relative remainder without normalising `..` (crates/effigy-exec/src/cwd.rs:45).

Probe results are now keyed by a typed ProbeKind whose interpreter owns the reading, so a result can no longer be looked up by its human description, and a container that answered neither shell probe reports no shell instead of /bin/sh; the dead tools map and compose_exec_args helper are gone (crates/effigy-exec/src/detection.rs:120).
Three typed exec refusals, each with the next action in its Display; consumers can match the variant instead of the text.
Crate surface and docs only; the module list and re-exports are the whole file.
The single owner of host/container routing: typed ExecTarget with a distinct not-running target, a documented rule order and one host-native command list.
Sole owner of the anonymous cleanup pin; the pipe's file type, owner uid and access mode are re-checked and only a duplicate may reach a workload.
The open reason now names itself as a stable string for the journal digest instead of deriving identity from Debug text (crates/effigy-kernel/src/ctx.rs:29).

Custody keeps the process core, anchor and platform seam, and the output pipeline now has its own owner; the per-intent digest is built from typed fields rather than Debug text, though 2,034 lines still carry spawn, capture and settlement (crates/effigy-kernel/src/custody.rs:14).
Sole owner of same-image anchor verdicts: generation, nonce, group membership and start order are each required evidence and an unproven anchor is a pre-exec refusal.
One writer for parsed, redacted, durably appended output; styles are published only after the plain bytes and a failed write marks the record incomplete.
Owns bounded rotating per-stream logs keyed by absolute offset; a reader resumes exactly and an expired position is reported, and I/O failure only changes capture metadata.
Owns the merged append destination installed before a child is released; a failed append is not acknowledged and the poison is sticky.
Exclusive, descriptor-relative moves and swaps that fail closed; there is deliberately no ordinary-rename fallback that could clobber a raced operator file.
One-time legacy cutover with provenance-typed trust decisions and no legacy payload read; large but single-purpose and only reachable under the admitted host-process gate.

New single owner of the secret-bearing output path: terminal controls are removed first, redaction runs on the visible bytes, each stream projection is redacted again, and a secret set with no reader-safe replacement byte blocks the capture instead of leaking (crates/effigy-kernel/src/custody/output.rs:12).
Sole owner of OS observations and generation-evidenced signals, including the documented macOS/pre-6.9 numeric check-and-signal window; a pidfd is never treated as group authority.
The only post-fork path: prepared buffers, async-signal-safe syscalls, blocked timeout signals and one terminal lease per leader; unsafe blocks carry their own SAFETY argument.
Presentation data only, published after the plain append and used only on an exact identity/offset/text match; an unrecognized style file is retained as operator data.

The single control sanitizer for secret-bearing output: unclassifiable bytes are dropped and redaction runs on the same frame a reader would show. Covered from custody/tests.rs redaction cases, not by an inline test module.

The test-only fault points: a thread-local scope, a named and nth arming form, and an environment channel for re-executed children, so a fault is armed at one crossing rather than globally (crates/effigy-kernel/src/fault.rs:172).

Scoped hooks for engine proofs that use the kernel as a dependency, available only behind the feature and never through an environment variable, restoring the prior hook even when it unwinds (crates/effigy-kernel/src/fault_injection.rs:11).

The fault-child bound now follows the child's own boundary-progress mark instead of a wall clock, so host load cannot be read as a hung child while a genuinely stalled one is still killed and reported (crates/effigy-kernel/src/faults/driver.rs:24).

The §12.3 supervisor matrix as model tests over the kernel primitives a run supervisor uses: the full cross product of front end, prior state, stop and attachment with a strict-fake effect (crates/effigy-kernel/src/faults/matrix.rs:40).

The fault-injection surface: typed effect/observe/cleanup contexts, a verified fixture executable and bounded waits, so every scenario shares one arming and recovery shape (crates/effigy-kernel/src/faults/mod.rs:32).

Oracles O1-O14 over a captured World, each returning how many subjects it judged so the driver refuses a vacuous pass, and each with a negative control that proves it can fail (crates/effigy-kernel/src/faults/oracles.rs:48).

The probe sampler now follows the probe's exit event within a measured 2 s ceiling instead of judging one instant past deadline plus slack, and its own test shows a delayed guard passing while a hung or 3 s-late guard still reports a survivor (crates/effigy-kernel/src/faults/scenarios.rs:1098).

What the oracles read: a read-only snapshot of one fault HOME after recovery plus the audit rows and fake logs written while it ran, with audit triggers as instruments and never authority (crates/effigy-kernel/src/faults/world.rs:19).

Sole owner of safe descriptor-relative files: it now names the trust rule each mode refusal broke (open_mode_message) and creates component chains no-follow (create_component_path) (crates/effigy-kernel/src/fs.rs:261).

One write_body owner now bounds every gate body at DIAG_MAX, dropping the descriptive fields before the fixed identity and refusing rather than reading as another holder, with a test that an oversized argv0 cannot grow the file (crates/effigy-kernel/src/gate.rs:852).
Owns the external-resource lease identity; the inode is the lease and the mount-assigned device number is explicitly not evidence (effigy#337).
A foreground gate body now goes through the same bounded writer as acquisition instead of its own length check, so the file bound has one owner (crates/effigy-kernel/src/gate/foreground.rs:66).
One owner of the three-category human rendering (Refused/Unavailable/Broken) and its next step, which every kernel error Display routes through.
Sole owner of identity encoding v1: typed CheckoutId/RunId/TaskId/ResourceId, canonical path and Unicode normalization, caller-supplied entropy, and collision refusal.

The richer read-only OS-fact owner (Observed results, typed start identities), but effigy-process/src/identity.rs independently implements the same boot and per-PID start identity readers for the same host facts.
Owns retained live-interpolation custody: a shared description lock, a verified binding, and removal only on the helper's exact settlement; a dead helper leaves binding and residue untouched.
Private inherited socketpair whose request tag binds one datagram's descriptors to its pipe control frame; refusal closes every received handle. One focused test.
Crate wiring and the fault_point! macro, which is an unconditional Ok outside fault-injection test builds; no behaviour of its own.
The checkout location is the identity (root path only); deliberately resolves no Git generation (Q-011). Passive type, exercised through the routing proofs.
Owns immutable file closures and role validation; publication and retention share one short store gate and every path component is validated before a byte is written.
The preflight seal never publishes or takes a gate; recovery removes a staging tree only on positive lease proof and an uninspectable lease leaves it untouched.
The Run-side publisher: one journalled intent, one objects gate, one reference transaction; a sealed receipt is re-verified under the gate before promotion.
Observed<T> keeps Verified/Absent/Unknown distinct with evidence and an absence proof that says what was proven; unknown never becomes an absence.
The one structured result: typed outcome/disposition/residue, and Invocation rejects shell-string reconstruction so argument grammar stays with the engine.
Small read-only probe surface: one deadline, ordered Observed results, and an explicit rule that a command exit is not a readiness fact.

The guard's deadline is now an explicit budget from now rather than the caller's remaining context, which removes the setup-latency coupling; the guard still keeps a second frame reader beside the new supervise codec (crates/effigy-kernel/src/probe/guard.rs:303).
Owns bounded HTTP/TCP/unix/DNS observation and the explicit status policy; malformed or oversized headers are Unknown, never ready.

The workload's own window now starts at release, after the fork and spawn barrier, so a scheduler-delayed setup can neither consume nor hide the probe deadline (crates/effigy-kernel/src/probe/process.rs:140).
Sole owner of atomic_replace (staged write, fsync, one rename), bounded typed reads, and the one-pointer multi-file commit; a decode failure is Unknown, never a default.
Owns in-band remote custody: typed container identity (id+created+vm_boot_id), nonce-bound registration, argv passed through sh -c "$@" rather than interpolated, and Unknown for every partial proof.
Fault-injection-only qualification case taxonomy (before-identity through foreign-session); it declares itself a runner shape, not real-engine QA credit.
Turns session snapshots into typed SessionState and distinguishes only inventory, boot-change and complete-session proofs as absence.
Bounded stream buffer with its own sequence and cursor accounting, consumed by the remote session records.

Bounded incremental retention that never removes an unsettled run, a referenced object or a live claim, with per-machine rate limiting. Default-suite proof is thin: the discriminating retention cases live in the fault-injection suite.

Owns the verified checkout and machine state roots, separate database names and the guest-placement refusal before any filesystem call, and reuses fs's one untrusted-mode message (crates/effigy-kernel/src/root.rs:134).
The one unreadable-checkout warning now goes through the bounded output owner instead of a raw eprintln (crates/effigy-kernel/src/root/checkout.rs:82).
Owns machine-gate routing and the private derived-file gate root, refusing non-host authority and never exposing a database from that root.
Runtime-location root opening (local journal per checkout) delegating every trust check to root.rs and fs.rs.
One gate spelling per checkout: a recorded token and the path-derived identity take the same lock, so foreground and durable runs of one task exclude each other.

The stored attachment mode now has one encoder and decoder (AttachMode::stored/decode_stored) instead of hand-written JSON literals in writers and the transition query (crates/effigy-kernel/src/run/attachments.rs:21).
Keeps the shared checkout lifetime protected through native process cleanup even after the checkout and journal are externally deleted.
Child admission as a parent intent: reuse of an id is refused before the intent and the parent link commits with Admitted, before the child's first effect.
Atomic machine facts: a complete conflict set rolls back foreign claims and generations, and a stale publication cannot advance the model.
A foreground admission now refuses more gates than the declared bound instead of growing its footprint with aliases (crates/effigy-kernel/src/run/foreground.rs:131).
Pure journal reads for status projections; nothing here repairs a run, probes a process or acquires a gate, and a stored phase is decoded into Phase.
Private journal-row access for the owner-gated Run API: fence and target checks precede any effect insert, and a stopping run refuses new intent.
The Run owner alone records custody identities and owns its death pipe; metadata readback is Observed.
Pure reads by absolute byte offset across rotation: expired bytes are reported, a failed capture surfaces as truncated, and nothing is silently skipped.

Machine completion records belong here, but this file also renders and appends the gateway operator event log (and calls the gateway-specific fs opener), which the gateway consumes; one owner should be the gateway.
Foreground intent/completion in memory only, with no store, filesystem, clock or process API reachable and explicit rules for Intended/Unknown/terminal transitions.

The run facade re-exports the terminal bounds the persistence contract now states; 2,781 lines still hold the journal, admission, attachments and settlement surface in one row (crates/effigy-kernel/src/run/mod.rs:35).
Bounded, redacted caller provenance whose only consumer is the gateway operator event log; 1,435 lines of diagnostic attribution sit in the run family rather than with the log's owner.
One recoverable settle: engines supply observations and undo, the policy keeps waiting for a busy store rather than losing an outcome, and residue is recorded with its own sequence.
Owns the run control socket path and connection; names are relative to a verified directory and the listener is bound before it is advertised.

The terminal record is now a bounded row: identities and closed-set words are validated and refused rather than cut, only the descriptive task label is truncated with a visible marker, and the insert/prune page and frame budgets are stated and enforced (crates/effigy-kernel/src/run/terminal.rs:42).

The kernel half of the workspace channel: replay-safe admission and per-client attachments, with a changed digest a conflict and an unresolvable reservation Unknown. Large because it holds both record families.

Unwired pre-effect capacity scaffold: every item is #[allow(dead_code)] and no name in the module is referenced outside it (Capacity has zero references in the crate); the module doc says the resident worker and custody do not exist yet. Its eight tests exercise only the scaffold.
One process-wide router installed once by the binary: the async handler only publishes bounded atomic facts, errno is preserved, and a second install is refused.
Binds a socket name relative to a verified directory without a process-wide chdir; long paths stay independent of the caller's cwd.

The store now reads back the settings that bound its side files and refuses an open whose bounds did not apply, and closes with a bounded truncating checkpoint instead of leaving an unbounded log (crates/effigy-kernel/src/store.rs:523).

The length-prefixed helper, event and owning-client frame codec now has one owner in frame.rs instead of three inline copies; 2,331 lines still carry the supervisor, channels and windowing (crates/effigy-kernel/src/supervise.rs:40).
The same-image group anchor: ready PID before go, exit on SIGTERM, retirement or empty group; its only substance is the evidence custody reads about it.

Explicitly scaffolding: module doc disclaims any helper capability and the module is declared with #[allow(dead_code)]; self_hash has no caller anywhere in the workspace, and its eight tests only exercise the hash cache.

New single owner for the length-prefixed frame codec with its own typed FrameError, wire bound, short-write and WouldBlock retry, partial-peer buffering and six tests (crates/effigy-kernel/src/supervise/frame.rs:53).
Qualification-only same-image verification; ordinary builds do not consume the observations and it is marked as such at its declaration.

The memory guard's acknowledgement and finish reads now use the one frame codec instead of four hand-rolled read loops, though it still duplicates the supervise read/write helpers beside it (crates/effigy-kernel/src/supervise/memory.rs:582).

3,851 lines own the wire, the TLS pin check, hello/version/digest negotiation, enrolment/authentication, the canonical request digest, replay ordering and five entry points; each part is individually sound but the file is not proportionate to a single module.

The workspace session facade now only documents the session's authority and re-exports its owners, with the reservation, claim, selection and serving mechanisms in their own modules (crates/effigy-kernel/src/workspace_session/mod.rs:47).

Owns the durable activation reservation a successor generation commits through, with typed decisions and refusals, frozen target evidence and a publication receipt that separates the ID difference as inference (crates/effigy-kernel/src/workspace_session/activation.rs:790).

Owns who may claim a reserved generation and the plan one claim commits, refusing a replayed, shared or widened claim from the same gate and reservation row (crates/effigy-kernel/src/workspace_session/claims.rs:128).
An inside-requested down is not a cascade: it refuses while any other holder is live or unknown, stops only the session's own children, then re-checks holders under a transition permit.
Guest-local fields are frozen before publication and every field is validated against those inputs rather than admitted from arbitrary document data.
Frozen image facts with a typed LoaderFamily observed in the image root, never inferred from the host or a staged executable.

The selection group keeps the durable guest selection one activation commits: typed state and liveness, the context document a client reads, and the obligation written in the same transaction that publishes active(E) (crates/effigy-kernel/src/workspace_session/selection/obligation.rs:42).
Owns the session's listener and memory-only key as typed values; ChannelBound is the only value that names a locator, so a listener is never advertised before it is bound.

Owns the environment's one session identity, its typed terminal and owner-loss vocabulary, the down it requested and the supervisor that consumes kernel records instead of keeping a second copy (crates/effigy-kernel/src/workspace_session/session.rs:490).
The transition's Borrow lookup now asks AttachMode for its stored text instead of matching a JSON literal (crates/effigy-kernel/src/workspace_session/transition.rs:52).
The only exit-diagnostic renderer, but it turns ExitStatus into the prose strings exit=N/signal=N that consumers parse back; a typed exit fact would keep the verdict out of text.

Typed boot/start identity with an explicit Unknown comparison that never classifies ambiguity as a different session, but it duplicates effigy-kernel's ident boot/start identity (crates/effigy-process/src/identity.rs:214).
The crate re-export surface now names ProcessTreeError so a caller can tell an unenumerated tree from a refused signal (crates/effigy-process/src/lib.rs:25).
Thin dispatch to the single spawn and terminate implementations; no policy of its own.
Attaches the two stream threads and the single exit watcher, but publishes the exit as the same prose payload that the TUI re-parses; keep one typed exit event.

Graceful child shutdown keeps its own deadline and states that the tree verdict belongs to the caller; only the now-Result signal calls are ignored explicitly (crates/effigy-process/src/lifecycle/shutdown.rs:8).
A second spawner with its own process-group discipline (pre_exec setpgid) beside kernel custody/spawn.rs; PTY and terminal-size handling are correct and the term-size guard refuses malformed sizes.
One poison-tolerant lock helper with its rationale: the guarded child handles stay usable after a panic, so recovery beats aborting every future signal.

One process-table snapshot now answers both the group and descendant questions, a malformed row refuses the whole snapshot rather than dropping a member, ESRCH is treated as absence instead of a refused signal, and an unread table is reported as unenumerated (crates/effigy-process/src/signal.rs:34).
The one bounded stream reader: it emits both raw chunks and decoded lines, keeps CRLF handling in one place and flushes a trailing partial line at EOF.
Best-effort tree signalling on control shutdown stays explicit about claiming no tree verdict (crates/effigy-process/src/supervisor_control.rs:32).
Small owned accessors; required_child_handle keeps the ProcessNotFound error that the control path should also use.
Shutdown proves the direct child's exit with try_wait and states that the tree signal it sends is best-effort (crates/effigy-process/src/supervisor_shutdown.rs:22).
